description: Three realistic prompts run against a synthetic fixture instance, with the skill (CLI) and without it (raw HTTP plus a hand-crafted Anchor). Results live in results/iteration-1/.

evals.name: read-feedback
evals.prompt: I'm reviewing feedback left on the fixture project's README.md. List the annotations on README.md and tell me what the human wants me to change. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A parsed annotation list and a short summary naming both human requests: mention Node 18+ before install, and replace the placeholder fox sentence with a real example.
expectations: The list output parses as a JSON array
Both seeded human annotations are returned
Every note exposes author alice and isAgent false
The answer names both requested changes
evals.baseline_notes: Raw HTTP can read this too; these assertions are non-discriminating by design.

evals.name: create-from-quote
evals.prompt: Create an annotation on README.md quoting 'fox jumps' and saying: 'Explain what the fox represents; this is a placeholder.' Use your author name claude.
evals.expected_output: An annotation whose first note is author claude, isAgent true, and whose Anchor is Active — the stored blockText is the rendered paragraph ('The quick brownfox jumps overthe lazy dog.'), not the raw wrapped source line.
expectations: The create response parses as JSON with an annotation id
The created note carries author claude and isAgent true
The stored anchor quotes the requested span
The CLI-computed anchor is Active (stored anchor equals the CLI builder on the same content)
Hard-wrapped prose projects to rendered text (soft breaks concatenate)
evals.baseline_notes: The no-skill baseline posts hand-crafted anchor JSON built from the raw source line; the server accepts it but it resolves Outdated (blockText 'fox jumps over').

evals.name: resolve-author
evals.prompt: Resolve every annotation authored by claude in the fixture project, then confirm none remain unresolved. Leave the human's annotations alone.
evals.expected_output: Both claude-authored annotations resolved, no unresolved claude threads left, and the alice-authored thread still unresolved.
expectations: The author filter returns only threads containing a claude note
Batch resolve updates exactly the claude annotations
Annotations from other authors stay unresolved
evals.baseline_notes: Raw HTTP can do this too; the assertions confirm the documented ?author= contract.
